question: Does a different owning semantic gate reject StepTermination values that carry faultCause or reasonCodes on the wrong class (and operational errorCode/faultCause mismatches), or is the shape-only admission a real contract/schema/reference gap?
summary: The retained D9 class/code law forbids every root-observed combination, and the successor explicitly retains that law while replacing the D9 union's per-variant field closure with StepTermination. No other owning gate applies it to a received termination. Every identified producer emits only lawful terminations by construction, so this is a published-carrier admission gap, not an observed unlawful emission.

producer.finding: All lawful by construction. None emits a required-illegal termination (probe p01: ROUTES 24/24, public_termination_for 22/22, terminate 23/23 lawful). Each producer validates only against the schema.

trustedHostFinalizer.finding: Derives the unique faultCause from errorCode, places reasonCodes only for indeterminate and checks exit, so faultCause/reasonCodes exclusivity and pairing hold by construction. It does not check the input code's legality for its class: it drops a code on success (28 of 28 enumerated success inputs with a code) and emits request-rejected with fault-family codes (11). Advisory A1/A2.

publicTypedEnvelope.finding: The published schema is the only admission. It admits all 13 required-illegal combinations at every referencing site (probe p01). No semantic gate applies class/code legality to a received termination.

importedRetained.finding: The invocation-record schemas admit all 13 combinations. No import kind carries a termination, and the retained Run closure holds none, so the schema is again the only admission.

dispositions.title: Restore cause/code exclusivity on the public carrier
dispositions.law: codeDerivation; X1; X3; X4; the succeeded hostTerminationUnion per-variant closure
dispositions.edit: In both common schemas' StepTermination branches: success and interrupted refuse faultCause and reasonCodes (success already refuses reasonCodes); policy-failed refuses reasonCodes and faultCause; request-rejected refuses reasonCodes and faultCause; operational-failed refuses reasonCodes; indeterminate refuses faultCause.
dispositions.why: Root's four combinations plus six same-law cases are admitted everywhere today. The D9 union refused the reasonCodes cases, and faultCause is a successor-added field whose only lawful class is operational-failed.

dispositions.title: Enforce operational-failed faultCause/errorCode pairing on the public carrier
dispositions.law: codeDerivation errorCode = map(cause); codeMaps total and injective ('a golden whose code disagrees with its axes fails D6'); successor host-invariant -> SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE (native §10, workflows_model FAULT_TO_ERROR)
dispositions.edit: The operational-failed branch gains anyOf over the 11 exact (faultCause, errorCode) pairs, plus a check_workflows control that the schema pairs equal workflows_model.FAULT_TO_ERROR in order.
dispositions.why: The successor carrier alone publishes both axes. A mismatch (HOST.IO_FAILURE + ledger-busy, CONFIG.INVALID + host-io, SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE + host-io) is a record that disagrees with itself under retained D9 law, and all three are admitted today. The D9 union could not enforce this because it had no faultCause field; the successor owns the surface it added.

dispositions.title: request-rejected errorCode restricted to the rejectionCauseToErrorCode image
dispositions.why: Retained law, but rejectionCause is not carried publicly and the D9 union typed errorCode without a class partition, so this was always a derivation obligation of the host finalizer (invariant-one-mapper), not boundary closure. Deliberately not in the diff; request-rejected + HOST.IO_FAILURE is still admitted after the edit (p03 advisoryStillAdmitted).

dispositions.title: Host public_termination should refuse, not drop or pass, a unit class/code that D9 forbids
dispositions.why: Observed: success with any code emits bare success; request-rejected accepts fault-family codes. §12 claims only exit and faultCause checks, so this is not a contradiction, just a narrower join than the retained law allows. Not a new blocker.

limits: No group or global suite was run. The new check_workflows control and the vectors were replicated narrowly in p03, not executed inside check_workflows.v1.py.
Pins, reports and the package manifest were not regenerated. I did not verify pin locations for workflow-cases.v1.json, check_workflows.v1.py or workflows-and-surfaces.md, which also change.
The retained-law predicate in probes/boundaries.py is my transcription of D9 codeDerivation/X1/X3/X4/codeMaps plus FAULT_TO_ERROR. Every verdict is reported beside the actual boundary outcome.
boundaries.py is shared by p01 and p03 and is not digest-recorded in the receipts (only each entry probe is). It changed once, by the p01 type-guard fix, before the passing runs.
The fixture scan covers JSON files only. Python-constructed terminations are covered through the enumerated producers and the inspected checks, not exhaustively.
Envelope boundaries were probed with kind=failure only. The graph-query and invocation-record sites were probed at the termination property pointer, not with whole documents.
public_termination was enumerated with one detail code (CONFIG.INVALID) over every class × {none, 19 error codes, 9 reason codes}.
Not assessed (outside class/code legality): signal on operational-failed; runId/coverageId/executionId placement; field closure otherwise owned by the successor.
The D9 v1.14 goldens are historical HostTermination values without faultCause. They were flagged by the pairing predicate only because that field is absent, and are unaffected.
